title: Automotive: 26.1M Completed Views at $0.0048 CPCV Across 7 Markets
excerpt: A global automotive marque launched its Asia brand film across seven markets with CPMs 85% under market rate. Read the case.
rm_desc: Automotive programmatic advertising across seven markets, CPMs 85% under market rate. Read the case.
content: This automotive programmatic advertising campaign covers a global automotive marque launching its Asia brand film across seven markets simultaneously, with distributor lead generation attached to a brand objective.
Planning automotive programmatic advertising across seven markets

AI-driven programmatic planning and buying ran across all seven markets at once, optimised to completed views against CPCV rather than impressions. Lead capture was routed to market distributors alongside the brand objective, and the buy was benchmarked market by market against local CPM norms, since a single regional average would have hidden which markets were actually delivering efficient inventory and which were quietly dragging the blended number down.

A brand film running in seven markets at once has seven different inventory markets, seven different audience behaviours, and seven different price floors to negotiate. Direct buys with individual publishers do not scale against that without a proportional increase in account management overhead. Automotive programmatic advertising bought through a demand-side platform lets the buy reallocate spend toward whichever market and placement is delivering completed views most efficiently in real time, rather than committing budget to seven markets up front and hoping the initial split turned out to be the right one.
26.1 million completed views at a $0.0048 CPCV, CPMs 85% under market rate, and 32,298 leads delivered to market distributors.

This was a brand campaign, so read those numbers as reach economics: completed views bought unusually cheaply at scale. View metrics do not translate directly into lead-gen unit costs, and the 32,298 leads were a secondary outcome of a film built for attention, not the primary objective the media plan was optimised against. Other automotive programmatic advertising campaigns built specifically for lead generation should be held to their own lead-gen benchmarks, not this one's CPCV.

A low CPCV on a global automotive brand film does not predict what a smaller, less recognisable brand would pay for similar inventory; auction dynamics favour brands with existing name recognition and creative assets that a platform's own quality signals have already learned to trust over time. Automotive programmatic advertising for a smaller challenger brand entering the same category cold would need its own independent benchmark, built carefully from its own test spend over several weeks, rather than simply assuming this particular campaign's favourable numbers as a realistic target from day one.

This campaign sat inside a broader paid media engagement; the full scope of what that covers is on our services page. Brands weighing automotive programmatic advertising against a more traditional direct-buy media plan across several markets at once can use this case as a starting benchmark for the conversation, not a guarantee.
How the budget was allocated across markets

Rather than splitting the budget evenly across seven markets on a fixed schedule, spend shifted weekly toward whichever markets and placements were producing completed views at the lowest CPCV, with a floor kept in every market so none went dark entirely. This meant the highest-performing two or three markets carried a disproportionate share of total spend by the campaign's midpoint, a pattern that would alarm a stakeholder expecting even, predictable delivery across every market, but is exactly what efficient automotive programmatic advertising is meant to do once the underlying performance data has accumulated enough signal to act on with real confidence.
Client described rather than named, and all figures are reported exactly as recorded at the time.
